anomaly_def.Name: Storage I/O Throughput Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description: Definition: Root cause located at the storage device or storage-virtualization layer, where the sustained rate of physical reads and writes saturates the throughput, IOPS, or latency budget of the underlying volumes used by data files, temporary files, log files, and backup destinations. It is distinct from the engine-level subsystems that submit I/O because the limiting factor is the physical capacity of the device rather than how the engine is configured. Observable phenomena: device-level wait time well above device service time, sharply rising read and write latency on the underlying volumes, queue depths pegged near their maximum, high database I/O wait while CPU utilization remains moderate, wait profiles dominated by data-file, temporary-file, log-file, buffer-I/O, and durability-flush events, and elongated batch windows and statement response times. Possible contributing factors: insufficient spindle count or insufficient provisioned IOPS, write penalties from the storage layout, asynchronous I/O disabled or filesystem read-ahead too small, mismatch between filesystem block size and database page size, hot data and log files concentrated on a single device, missing flash or solid-state caching tier, virtualization or shared-storage neighbor contention, and storage-controller or path-failure events degrading throughput.

entry.error_class: Class 42 - Syntax Error or Access Rule Violation
entry.cause_analysis: The failure is typically associated with unsupported syntax, invalid statement structure, or feature usage that the target engine version cannot execute as written.
entry.solution_guidance: Validate SQL syntax, target-engine compatibility, statement shape, and whether the feature is supported under the current engine version or execution context.
